title: Re-registration in the National Population Register on return to Norway
description: On moving back to Norway, the returnee must report the move to Skatteetaten (folkeregisteret) as a move to Norway (flytting til Norge). For returning nationals this is usually done in person at a tax office with valid ID; it re-establishes a registered address and national-ID status and restores access to public services and BankID.

title: Re-establishing Norwegian tax residence
description: Norwegian tax residence is re-established when presence exceeds 183 days in any 12-month period or 270 days in any 36-month period; a returning long-term national is typically resident from the date of return. The timing must be reconciled with the closing of French residence to avoid a double-residence gap or period of dual taxation.

title: Re-affiliation to National Insurance (folketrygden) via NAV
description: Membership of folketrygden generally resumes on becoming resident or working in Norway again. Any voluntary-membership arrangement used while abroad should be closed, and continuity of insurance periods documented so that EEA aggregation of the French period is preserved for pension purposes.

title: French tax exit - declaration de depart to DGFiP
description: Leaving France requires notifying the French tax authority (DGFiP) of the departure via impots.gouv.fr, filing a final French income-tax return covering the period of residence, and settling any exit obligations. Failure leaves the mover on the French tax roll and risks continued resident-fiscal treatment and duplicate taxation.

title: CPAM deregistration and closing French health cover
description: The returnee must notify CPAM of the departure, stop using the Carte Vitale once cover ends, and close any S1 / A1 arrangement. If he remained on Norwegian social security via an S1 while in France, that S1 must be surrendered to Helfo/NAV on return to avoid duplicate coverage records.
evidence_quote: Ainsi avant votre départ, vous devez restituer à votre caisse d'assurance maladie en France, votre carte Vitale et votre carte européenne d'assurance maladie (CEAM) ainsi que celles de vos enfants mineurs qui partent avec vous.

title: Pension portability - frozen French rights, reactivated Norwegian accrual
description: French basic (CNAV) and complementary (Agirc-Arrco) pension rights accrued during the assignment are preserved and payable at retirement age; they are not transferred. Under EEA aggregation each country pays a pro-rata pension. Norwegian OTP and folketrygd accrual resumes on return. The mover should keep French pension statements and his French social-security number.
evidence_quote: Quelle que soit votre situation, les droits que vous avez déjà acquis précédemment sont conservés sur votre compte de points retraite.

title: Retaining a French bank account as a non-resident
description: French banks such as BNP Paribas and LCL can convert a resident account to a compte non-resident rather than requiring closure. Keeping one open eases receipt of French pension, tax refunds and residual bills, but the bank must be notified of the change of residence and tax status and the FATCA/CRS self-certification updated.

title: Re-importing a vehicle to Norway (one-off tax and VAT)
description: Bringing a vehicle into Norway (outside the EU customs union) requires a customs declaration to Tolletaten and can trigger the one-off registration tax (engangsavgift) and 25% VAT, unless a duty relief for removal goods of a returning resident applies. This is a frequently underestimated cost on repatriation.

title: Removal goods FR to NO - customs declaration and relief
description: Household effects moved from France (EU) to Norway (non-EU) must be declared to Norwegian customs (Tolletaten). Duty and VAT relief for flyttegods (removal goods of a person moving to Norway) is available with an inventory and evidence of prior foreign residence and ownership period.

title: Re-enrolling in Norwegian healthcare and a regular GP (fastlege)
description: On resuming folketrygden membership the returnee regains Helfo coverage and should register with a regular GP (fastlege) via helsenorge.no. There can be a short qualifying or registration gap, so private travel cover during the transition is advisable.
evidence_quote: All inhabitants who are registered in the National Population Register as living in Norway have the right to a General Practitioner/family doctor.

title: Children: school / barnehage re-enrolment and barnetrygd
description: Returning children must be re-enrolled in Norwegian school or barnehage (managed by the municipality), and barnetrygd (child benefit) re-applied for with NAV once resident. French CAF benefits must be stopped to avoid overlap and clawback.

title: Trailing French tax on retained French property
description: If the returnee keeps French property, France retains taxing rights on French-source rental income and on any future capital gain (plus-value immobiliere), and taxe fonciere remains due. He files as a non-resident with DGFiP, with NO-FR treaty relief against Norwegian worldwide taxation.
